title: Reduction of an affine family before flatness
statement: Let X be an affine scheme, f:X → T a locally finite type morphism [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], V an affine open of T containing the image of f, and η a generic point of T in V. There exist integral affine S [def-pc-integral-scheme], reduced affine Z [def-pc-reduced-scheme], and universal homeomorphisms [def-weil-universal-homeomorphism] q:S → V and h:Z → X ×_T S [def-pc-fibre-product]. The composite Z → S is locally of finite type. Here S → T is q followed by the inclusion of V. No flatness or finite presentation is required.

source.place: Tag 0559, second proof, reduction paragraph; Tags 01IZ and 054M

proof.text: Take S to be the reduction of V. The reduction theorem makes S reduced and q a surjective closed immersion. Lift η through q and reflect specialization along q and V → T to prove the lift generic, making S irreducible and integral. Affineness follows from the closed immersion into affine V.

The pullback of X to V is isomorphic to X because the image of f is in V. Pullback pasting shows P = X ×_T S is affine. Take Z to be the reduction of P. The reduction theorem makes Z reduced and h a surjective closed immersion, hence affine and universally homeomorphic. The map Z → S is locally finite type by composition of h with the base change of f.

proof_origin.note: Concrete construction and restriction argument, including pullback comparisons; generic flatness is applied separately in the parent module.

theorem exists_affine_reduction_preparation
    {X T : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine X] (f : X ⟶ T) [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    (V : T.Opens) (hV : IsAffineOpen V) (himage : Set.range f ⊆ V)
    (η : T) (hη : IsGenericPoint η Set.univ) (hηV : η ∈ V) :
    ∃ (S Z : Scheme.{u}) (q : S ⟶ V.toScheme)
      (h : Z ⟶ pullback f (q ≫ V.ι)),
      IsAffine S ∧ IsIntegral S ∧ IsAffine Z ∧ IsReduced Z ∧
      IsUniversalHomeomorphism q ∧ IsUniversalHomeomorphism h ∧
      LocallyOfFiniteType (h ≫ pullback.snd f (q ≫ V.ι))
